question: What are all the minimum requirements in Section 2 (pages 4–5) of the City of Hartford MERF general investment consultant RFP?
expected_facts: Section2 requires: (1) at least ten years providing general consulting; (2) senior leadership together at least three years; (3) no subcontracting account management, and all responsible personnel are employees; (4) currently consulting for at least five public pension funds each over $1.5bn; (5) primary consultant has at least five years of defined-benefit public-pension consulting and at least three years employed by proposer; (6) fiduciary service to MERF/OPEB and written compliance with their investment policies/guidelines; (7) no existing or potential material conflicts with the City Treasurer/staff, Pension Commission, OPEB Committee, actuary, auditor, managers or other providers; (8) agree to execute a contract similar to AppendixE; (9) current SEC investment-adviser registration; (10) carry or have applied by submission for general liability $5m, E&O/professional liability $5m, fiduciary liability $1m, workers' compensation/employer liability $1m, and cybersecurity $1m. Section2 says all qualifications must be met by March15,2024 at 5pm ET and AppendixA certification must be completed. AppendixA separately uses different client-threshold/history and insurance-date wording; this answer follows Section2 as asked.
acceptance: Require all ten Section2 bullet requirements and five insurance limits when asking 'all'. If the question retains whole-document scope, allow explanation of Section2 versus AppendixA differences rather than forcing a single contradictory date or >/$1.5bn threshold.

question: List the core functions that the City of Creve Coeur Employee Pension Plan expects from its pension fund consultant in its May 2020 RFP.
expected_facts: (1) Help develop and maintain the investment policy statement; (2) plan asset allocations annually and monitor regularly; (3) recommend changes when markets change significantly and flag concerns; (4) provide research and recommendations for investments in each asset class; (5) follow recommended investments closely and meet the Pension Board quarterly in person, and monthly or as needed by phone; (6) provide monthly reporting of portfolio performance and statements; (7) work with City staff on sourcing funds, opening new accounts and tracking liquidity for pension payments; (8) work with investment managers, funds and custodians to ensure timely year-end and quarterly reporting.
acceptance: Accept all eight functions summarized. Quarterly in-person meetings plus monthly/as-needed phone contact is correct; exact punctuation is not required.

question: Under the ILPA ESG Assessment Framework, how often does a GP review its ESG policy at the 'Intermediate' and at the 'Advanced' level of the 'Approach to Policy Review' component?
expected_facts: Intermediate: the GP reviews its ESG policy periodically, i.e. every 2-3 years, and can share recent findings and updates. Advanced: the GP reviews its ESG policy annually and can comment on its evolution.

question: What topics does the ILPA DDQ 2.0 cover under its ESG section?
expected_facts: Section19 has seven subsections: 19.1 Policy—ESG policies, governance and oversight; 19.2 Fundraising—ESG commitments in fund documentation; 19.3 Pre-investment—material ESG risks/opportunities and due diligence; 19.4 Post-investment—portfolio-company mitigation, value creation and monitoring; 19.5 Reporting and Disclosure—LP monitoring/reporting and material incidents; 19.6 Climate Change—GHG measurement/reporting, commitments/actions and TCFD reporting; 19.7 Additional Information—other ESG topics/practices not otherwise covered and management-company internal ESG risks/opportunities and performance.
acceptance: Seven subsection groups, including Additional Information and management company's own ESG. Examples under each group are optional; do not treat six as the complete count.

acceptance: Require total 31% and 10% PE / 7% private debt / 10% real estate / 4% infrastructure. Consultant/advisor counts and core/non-core splits are optional.

question: A real assets investment consulting solicitation states that the funds' strategic asset allocation targets were adopted by the Board in 2003. As of September 30, 2010, how much did the Board have in its separate account private real estate program, its separate account private infrastructure program, and public real estate securities, and how large were its unfunded commitments?

acceptance: Accept approximately $164m/$59m/$25m/$88m mapped to the four requested categories. Issuer, solicitation number and total $4.2bn fund size are optional.

question: In the published questions and answers for a city's pension fund consulting RFP, the city says it sent the RFP to 21 firms and last ran such a search in 2013. What does the plan currently pay for advisory services on its equities and for management of its fixed income?
expected_facts: $20K per year for advisory of the equity investments (about 70% of plan funds, held by Fiduciary Advisors); for the fixed income investments (about 30% of plan funds, held by Commerce Bank, the custodian and paying agent) 0.30% on the first $10M, 0.20% on the next $40M and 0.15% on the remaining balance. Issuer: City of Creve Coeur, MO.
acceptance: $20,000 annually plus 0.30% first $10m, 0.20% next $40m and 0.15% remainder. Basis-point equivalents 30/20/15 are acceptable. Provider names and 70/30 allocation are optional.

question: A sample investment management RFP for a domestic equity small cap growth mandate sets portfolio guidelines. What are the limits on single-issuer holdings, foreign issuers and cash, and which index must the portfolio outperform?
expected_facts: No more than 5% of the portfolio (at time of purchase) in any single issuer other than the Federal Government/Agencies or the designated cash reserve fund; no more than 20% in foreign issuers, which must trade on the NYSE, ASE or NASDAQ; cash and equivalents no more than 10% except during cash withdrawals or contributions; the portfolio is expected to outperform the Russell 2000 Growth Index, net of fees. Issuer: Illinois Municipal Retirement Fund (IMRF) sample RFP.
acceptance: Accept equivalent 5% single-issuer at purchase, 20% foreign listed on specified US exchanges, 10% cash, and Russell 2000 Growth net-of-fee target. Preserve material exceptions; issuer identification is optional.

question: An investment manager RFP template for an emerging markets equity strategy (issued February 14, 2022, responses due March 31, 2022) lists required minimum qualifications and 'preferred criteria'. What live track record does it require, and what public pension client base does it prefer?
expected_facts: Required: an established (live) track record of at least 5 years managing the proposed emerging markets equity strategy (qualified women-, minority- or disabled-owned businesses are exempt). Preferred: at least two existing U.S. public pension fund clients with over $1 billion in total plan assets, or at least one existing public plan client with over $10 billion in total plan assets (plus no material litigation in the past five years). Issuer: State Universities Retirement System of Illinois (SURS).
acceptance: Accept five-year live strategy record and the alternative client tests (two >$1bn U.S. public pensions OR one >$10bn public plan). Ownership exemption is a relevant qualification. Issuer, litigation criterion and placeholder date need not be volunteered.

acceptance: Three factors with substantively equivalent descriptions suffice; exact wording and order are unnecessary.

question: What minimum qualifications must an audit firm meet in the Kern County Employees' Retirement Association (KCERA) RFP for audit services?
expected_facts: (1) Professional public accounting firm organized at least on a regional basis providing audit and attest services; (2) within the last five years, at least five audits of defined benefit pension plans with assets over $2 billion; (3) experience auditing equity securities (domestic and foreign), fixed income, real estate, alternative investments, commodities and securities lending; (4) an established office in the United States; (5) independent, licensed by and in good standing with California under the Accountancy Act; (6) Engagement Partner (and signing partner) located in the U.S. with at least 10 years of public accounting experience including DB pension plan audits, California-licensed CPA; (7) Engagement Manager located in the U.S. with at least 5 years of public accounting experience including DB plan audits, CPA licensed in a U.S. state; (8) On-Site Audit Supervisor located in the U.S. with at least 3 years of auditing experience including DB plan audits, CPA licensed in a U.S. state; (9) Engagement Manager and Supervisor available for consultations and in-person meetings throughout the year.
acceptance: Accept a faithful summary of the nine requirements. Do not impose desirable two audits of >$3bn plans or a California license for manager/supervisor as minimums; a U.S.-state license suffices for those roles.

question: What scope of services does the Kern County Employees' Retirement Association (KCERA) 2024 actuarial audit services RFP require?
expected_facts: A full actuarial audit of the assumptions, methods, calculations and experience used in KCERA's valuation, in two parts: (1) a peer review audit of the Actuarial Experience Study for July 1, 2019 - June 30, 2022 and the Review of Economic Actuarial Assumptions as of June 30, 2022 - evaluating the data (including comparison of census data), reconciling discrepancies with the consulting actuary, and evaluating the recommended economic and non-economic assumptions; and (2) a parallel valuation (independent reproduction) of the June 30, 2023 valuation, including the SRBR valuation and GASB 67 valuation, using the consulting actuary's assumptions and methods and reproducing all work without relying on the consulting actuary, with reconciliation of discrepancies. Results of both are to be communicated to the consulting actuary before completion of the June 30, 2024 valuation.
acceptance: Require both experience-study peer review and independent June 30, 2023 parallel valuation, including SRBR/GASB67 and discrepancy reconciliation. A concise account may group data and assumption checks; sample-agreement delivery details are optional.

question: In the INREV Due Diligence Questionnaire for Non-Listed Real Estate Investment Vehicles (2018), which expense ratio must the manager provide under Fees and Expenses, and on what bases?
expected_facts: Question 1.6.2 asks for the INREV Total Expense Ratio (TER): a forward-looking estimate (with the calculation method) if the vehicle has not been launched, or the INREV TER if it is an existing vehicle. question: What does the ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0 ask about GP-led secondaries and continuation funds in Section 6?
expected_facts: Section 6.0 opens with two Yes/No screening questions. 6.1 asks whether the Firm has done a GP-led secondary in the last five years, and 6.2 asks the same for a continuation fund transaction. Each has four follow-ups: did the LPAC review conflicts in every transaction; was a status quo option available to existing LPs in every transaction; was GP carry rolled over at 100% in every transaction; and were portfolio companies in an IPO or pre-IPO process excluded. Narrative questions 6.3-6.11 then cover: how conflicts of interest are reviewed with the LPAC and LPs (timing, information, Firm benefits not accruing to LPs, transparency on LPAC members or affiliates acting as acquirers); the information given to the LPAC/LPs and its timing; how new fund documents and side letters are structured; the options offered to LPs, including status quo, and differences for new or 'rolling' LPs; the impact on GP economics, alignment of interests and Key Person provisions; the rationale for this route rather than a fund extension or traditional exit; how the bidding universe and valuations are set (secondary managers, third-party advisers, valuation providers); fee structuring (broken deal/termination fees, sharing of transaction costs, management fee, carry); and disclosure of related deals between the GP and acquirers (e.g. stapled transactions or side deals).
acceptance: Accept a concise summary covering transaction history, four screening follow-ups, conflicts/disclosure and information, legal/economic/LP options, rationale, bidding/valuation, fees/carry and related deals. Exact subquestion numbering and every illustrative detail are optional.

Narrative questions 6.3-6.11 then cover: how conflicts of interest are reviewed with the LPAC and LPs (timing, information, Firm benefits not accruing to LPs, transparency on LPAC members or affiliates acting as acquirers); the information given to the LPAC/LPs and its timing; how new fund documents and side letters are structured; the options offered to LPs, including status quo, and differences for new or 'rolling' LPs; the impact on GP economics, alignment of interests and Key Person provisions; the rationale for this route rather than a fund extension or traditional exit; how the bidding universe and valuations are set (secondary managers, third-party advisers, valuation providers); fee structuring (broken deal/termination fees, sharing of transaction costs, management fee, carry); and disclosure of related deals between the GP and acquirers (e.g. stapled transactions or side deals).
acceptance: Accept a concise summary covering transaction history, four screening follow-ups, conflicts/disclosure and information, legal/economic/LP options, rationale, bidding/valuation, fees/carry and related deals. Exact subquestion numbering and every illustrative detail are optional.

question: What questions are asked under section 10.0 'ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance)' of the NJEDA Life Science Seed Fund due diligence questionnaire (Appendix A)?
expected_facts: Eight questions: 10.1 the role of the respondent's internal advisory board(s), all matters referred to them (including unresolved ones) and any other governing/advisory bodies; 10.2 conflicts of interest (potential, current, historic) and how they are identified, managed, disclosed (e.g. to the LPAC) and resolved, including any conflict committees; 10.3 the policy on personal investments by employees or affiliates in deals the respondent reviewed; 10.4 whether the respondent is a registered investment advisor (RIA); 10.5 the respondent's ESG-related policies and how ESG factors influence its investment beliefs; 10.6 the implementation status of its responsible investment policy and any plans to develop its approach to ESG; 10.7 how it contributes to portfolio companies' management of ESG risks and opportunities; 10.8 the monitoring processes it would use to assess the proposed Fund's portfolio companies' management of ESG factors.
acceptance: Eight topics 10.1–10.8 required in substance, including portfolio-company ESG assistance and monitoring. Exact question wording and numbering are optional.
